outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles, or moves a case of, the Margulis measure-classification conjecture as the bullet states it; the in-window work I found is on neighbouring problems (horospherical measures, bounded and dense orbits, uniform Littlewood, function-field orbit closedness, Anosov-action rigidity), plus one OpenAI-catalogue family (015, Sept–Oct 2026) proving Haar-equidistribution of torus packets with a measure-rigidity step, which is an analogue rather than a classification of diagonal-invariant measures.
problem_asks: (1) Setting: a higher-rank diagonalizable (diagonal or Cartan) action, of a group A of rank at least 2, on a homogeneous space G/Γ. The bullet says only higher-rank groups; it names no G, Γ or entropy hypothesis. (2) Claim: every ergodic A-invariant probability measure μ in that setting is algebraic, meaning it is the invariant measure on a closed orbit L·x of a closed subgroup L containing A (the conclusion in both the explicit and general forms below). (3) Scope the bullet implies: all such A and all such quotients, with no entropy hypothesis, since the bullet adds none. (4) The bullet links to the Grigory Margulis biography, not to a page on the conjecture. The explicit form that I could pin to a primary source is Conjecture 1.1 of Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss (arXiv math/0612721): for k≥3, every ergodic A-invariant probability measure on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z), with A the positive diagonal group, is algebraic. The general form is Conjecture 4 of Einsiedler's survey (arXiv 2101.11114), attributed to Furstenberg, Katok–Spatzier and Margulis: for a linear algebraic Q-group G and Γ = G(O_S), an ergodic A-invariant μ (no entropy assumption) is either virtually homogeneous, or there is a Q-subgroup L and a proper normal Q-subgroup H of L with conditions (1)–(3). Which of these the bullet denotes is for the judging pass; I have recorded both.

events.what_happened: Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss, 'Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture' (arXiv math/0612721). States Margulis's Conjecture 1.1 (for k≥3, every ergodic A-invariant probability measure on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z) is algebraic) and proves it under a positive-entropy hypothesis as Theorem 1.3: some one-parameter subgroup of A acts on X with positive entropy. Deduces that the exceptional set in Littlewood's conjecture has Hausdorff dimension zero.
events.revisions: The month is read from the arXiv identifier 0612; the abstract page was not opened, so the day is not pinned. Search results give Annals of Mathematics as the journal version; not opened.
events.delivers: The positive-entropy case of the SL_k case of the conjecture: for k≥3 and A the positive diagonal group, every ergodic A-invariant probability measure on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z) with positive entropy for some one-parameter subgroup of A is algebraic (an invariant measure on a single closed orbit of a closed connected L strictly containing A).
events.remains: The zero-entropy case for SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z) with k≥3 (Conjecture 1.1 as stated carries no entropy hypothesis); every homogeneous space and group in the bullet's general wording.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture's conclusion (algebraicity) under an added positive-entropy hypothesis, for the SL_k case; the direction the conjecture points.

sources: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/math/0612721 (introduction, Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.3 read; the acknowledgements were not reached)

events.what_happened: Einsiedler and Lindenstrauss, 'Symmetry of entropy in higher rank diagonalizable actions and measure classification' (arXiv 1803.07762). Per the abstract: for measures invariant under higher-rank diagonalizable actions, if the entropy along coarse Lyapunov foliations lacks a stronger analogous symmetry, the measure must be invariant under a nontrivial unipotent group. Search results give Journal of Modern Dynamics 2018 as the journal version; not opened.
events.delivers: A conditional structural dichotomy: an entropy-symmetry condition forces invariance under a unipotent group. It is not a classification of measures for the diagonal action.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: the paper gives the conditional dichotomy, not the classification.
events.direction: Points toward the classification by forcing unipotent invariance under an entropy-symmetry condition; it does not decide the conjecture.

sources: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1803.07762 (first 100,000 of about 121,000 characters read; no AI term found; the acknowledgements were not reached)

events.what_happened: An and Weiss, 'Remarks on minimal sets and conjectures of Cassels, Swinnerton-Dyer, and Margulis' (arXiv 1212.0216). Recasts Margulis's Conjecture 1 (for SL_n(R)/SL_n(Z), n≥3: every relatively compact orbit of the positive diagonal group A is closed) as equivalent assertions about compact minimal sets. It does not resolve the conjecture. This is a different Margulis conjecture from the measure one.
events.delivers: Equivalences only: the bounded-orbit closedness statement is equivalent to assertions about compact A-minimal sets. No case of it is established.
events.remains: The bounded-orbit closedness statement itself (still stated as open in the function-field paper of 2025, and not settled in any source I read). It is not a measure-classification question.
events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation with no resolution.

events.what_happened: Brown and Lee, 'Positive entropy actions by higher-rank lattices' (arXiv 2409.05991; v1 9 Sep 2024; v2 22 Jan 2025). Smooth actions of lattices in higher-rank simple Lie groups on compact manifolds, with positive topological entropy for one element. For SL(n,R)-lattices acting on n-manifolds the lattice is commensurable with SL(n,Z) (abstract). Theorem 2.3 builds an A-invariant measure on the suspension space that projects to Haar on G/Γ and has positive fiber entropy for some a in A.
events.delivers: Rigidity of smooth lattice actions on manifolds (Zimmer-program type). Its measure statement lives on a suspension space and is an existence result. It is not a classification of A-invariant ergodic measures on G/Γ.
events.direction: Neighbouring. It has a measure statement with a diagonal A, but it neither classifies nor denies the bullet's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kleinbock and Wu, 'Simultaneously bounded and dense orbits for commuting Cartan actions' (arXiv 2509.05272; submitted 5 Sep 2025; one version). On X₃ = SL₃(R)/SL₃(Z), the set of points with a bounded orbit under one regular diagonal flow and a dense orbit under a commuting diagonal flow has full Hausdorff dimension (Theorem 1.2). Motivated by the uniform Littlewood conjecture of Bandi–Fregoli–Kleinbock.
events.delivers: Full Hausdorff dimension of a set defined by bounded and dense orbit behaviour under commuting diagonal flows on SL₃(R)/SL₃(Z). The quantity is the dimension of an orbit set, not a measure.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: the set's dimension says nothing about the classification of invariant ergodic measures.
events.direction: Neighbouring. It uses diagonal flows on the same space, but the quantity is different.

events.what_happened: Huang and Shi, 'Bounded diagonal orbits in homogeneous spaces over function fields' (arXiv 2504.17644; v1 24 Apr 2025; v3 5 Jun 2025). The diagonal group of SL₄ over a Laurent-series function field has a non-closed relatively compact orbit (Theorem 1.2). The HTML gives characteristic 3, 5, 7 or 11; the abstract page says characteristic 3. The real case SL_n(R)/SL_n(Z) is discussed only as context (the Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer / Margulis conjecture).
events.delivers: A counterexample to closedness of relatively compact diagonal orbits over positive-characteristic function fields. It says nothing over R.
events.remains: The real case (the An–Weiss / Margulis bounded-orbit statement) and the measure-classification question. Both are untouched.
events.direction: Against the function-field analogue of the bounded-orbit form of the Margulis statement. The real case and the bullet's measure statement are not addressed.
events.object: A non-closed relatively compact D-orbit in SL₄(K)/SL₄(F[t]), for K a function field of characteristic 3, 5, 7 or 11 (Theorem 1.2, per the HTML). Existence is proved; the orbit is not written down in the parts I read.

events.what_happened: Schleischitz, 'Disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture' (arXiv 2603.12611; submitted 13 Mar 2026; one version). Shows that the uniform Littlewood conjecture of Bandi–Fregoli–Kleinbock is false. The counterexample pairs form a dense G_δ set and the supremum bound exceeds 1/188 (HTML Theorem 1.1). Follow-up preprints exist (arXiv 2607.08114, 9 Jul 2026; 2608.24401 and 2608.25059, found in search only, not opened).
events.delivers: Disproves the uniform Littlewood conjecture, a stronger uniform form. It does not decide Littlewood's conjecture itself, which the measure conjecture implies (EKL Conjecture 1.1 implies Littlewood).
events.direction: Against a uniform variant; a neighbour in the Littlewood chain, not the bullet's problem.

disputes.summary: 'Margulis conjecture' names several different statements in the sources read: (a) the measure-classification conjecture in the bullet (EKL Conjecture 1.1; survey Conjecture 4); (b) the bounded-orbit closedness conjecture for SL_n(R)/SL_n(Z), n≥3 (An–Weiss; Huang–Shi); (c) the injectivity-radius conjecture proved by Frączyk–Gelander; (d) the Margulis–Platonov conjecture (OpenAI family 018). 'Margulis measures' (Buzzi et al.) is a further namesake. I have treated only (a) as the bullet's problem, and recorded the others as neighbours or namesakes.

Press coverage of the OpenAI batch reports that OpenAI pulled three preprints after a sign error invalidated one argument and the constructions in two dependent papers, and revised fourteen others. The withdrawn items are not named in the sources read, so I cannot say whether family 015 was among them. The current catalogue has 719 manuscripts against 722 at the pinned commit.

summary: The bullet is Wikipedia's 'Margulis conjecture – measure classification for diagonalizable actions in higher-rank groups', in the Dynamical systems section of the live Wikipedia page (I read the live page, not the frozen 26 January 2024 revision). Its link goes to the Margulis biography, and the page gives no status. The explicit form I could pin to a primary source is Conjecture 1.1 of Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss (arXiv math/0612721): for k≥3 every ergodic A-invariant probability measure on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z), with A the positive diagonal group, is algebraic. Their Theorem 1.3 proves this under a positive-entropy hypothesis. Einsiedler's survey (arXiv 2101.11114, read through the ar5iv HTML because the PDF was unreadable) states the general Conjecture 4 without an entropy hypothesis, attributed to Furstenberg, Katok–Spatzier and Margulis, and calls the related Furstenberg measure question a notoriously hard open problem. The nearest pre-window advance is Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss (arXiv 2307.04163, 9 July 2023): a positive-entropy classification for arithmetic quotients of forms of SL_2^k and PGL_2^k, with an adelic entropy-free version under extra conditions (A2) and (A3). It leaves open the solvable alternative in the theorem. The authors' 2026 Stockholm talk (11 Sept 2026, SL_2(R)^r) mentions extensions with Shem-Tov and Wieser 'in progress'; I found no preprint. Since 26 January 2024 I found nothing that proves the general conjecture, removes the entropy hypothesis for SL_k with k≥3, or settles the zero-entropy case. The in-window items I opened are all neighbours: Choi–Kim (horospherical, unipotent, 2025 teaser and 2026 full paper), Brown–Lee (positive-entropy lattice actions on manifolds; its measure statement lives on a suspension and is an existence claim), Kleinbock–Wu (dimension of bounded/dense orbit sets for commuting diagonal flows on SL_3), Huang–Shi (non-closed bounded diagonal orbits over function fields, real case untouched), Schleischitz (disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture), and Buzzi et al. (Margulis measures on expanding foliations, a namesake). The one in-window item near the topic that uses a measure-rigidity step is in the OpenAI 'openai/math' catalogue, family 015 (three manuscripts dated 24 Sept and 5 Oct 2026): Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields, of prime degree ≥5 (plus quartic and sextic cases). I judge it an analogue, not a case: its limits are periodic torus-packet measures, not A-invariant ergodic measures of a diagonal action. But the family entry says 'the proof combines measure rigidity with a cubic-resolvent estimate', and I could not identify the theorem or group used, because the PDFs could not be read through WebFetch. Its Lean file DukePrimeDegree.lean has sorry in both top-level theorems. Its universal wording ('for any sequence of full lattices whose multiplier-order discriminants tend to infinity') sits uneasily with ELMV's stated examples of sequences of periodic orbits that fail to equidistribute, and the packet definition or the prime-degree restriction may be what avoids them; this is unverified. The catalogue credits 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' with 'the vast majority' of its results, which is not family-specific. I read the whole catalogue CONTENTS file (families 001–377) by keyword: the only Margulis-named entries are 018 (Margulis–Platonov, a namesake), and none of the twelve 'dynamical systems and ergodic theory' families (143–154) concerns this conjecture. Across 48 web searches and the opened sources, no AI system is tied to a claimed result on this conjecture. Close calls: whether 015 counts as a case of the bullet (I lean no, as an analogue); whether the bullet means the SL_k form or the general form (both recorded); and whether the 2023 Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss result is in scope (it predates the window).
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading: (a) read the bullet as the general measure-classification problem and treat family 015 as a movement on it, because it is a Haar-type classification of limits, it uses a measure-rigidity input, and it is in-window; against this, its objects are periodic torus-packet measures, not A-invariant ergodic measures, and the entry does not say a measure-rigidity theorem for a diagonal A is established. (b) Read the bullet as the bounded-orbit Margulis conjecture (An–Weiss), in which case Huang–Shi (2025) is an in-window event that settles a function-field analogue; against this, the bullet says 'measure classification', and the real case is untouched. (c) Count the 2023 Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss theorem as the operative state of the art, so that any in-window extension (Einsiedler's 2026 SL_2(R)^r talk) would count as progress; against this, no in-window preprint has been found.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The PDFs of OpenAI family 015 (prime, quartic and sextic): which measure-rigidity theorem they cite, for which A and which space, and whether the 'any sequence' claim is restricted in a way that avoids ELMV's non-equidistribution examples. (2) The Lean status of the quartic and sextic manuscripts, and whether DukePrimeDegree.lean's two sorry statements are filled. (3) Any arXiv preprint behind Einsiedler's 11 Sept 2026 SL_2(R)^r talk, or the Shem-Tov–Wieser extensions. (4) The acknowledgements of 2307.04163 and 1803.07762, which were not reached. judgement.why: The statement asks for classification of ergodic invariant measures for higher-rank diagonalizable actions on homogeneous spaces. Only EKL 2006 settles a restriction of that question (positive-entropy measures on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z), k≥3): a pre-snapshot case. Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss 2018 is a conditional dichotomy, not a classification of any class, so none. Every in-window item answers a different question: horospherical (unipotent) measures, lattice actions on manifolds, orbit-set dimension, function-field bounded orbits, uniform Littlewood, and namesakes (injectivity radius, Margulis–Platonov, Margulis measures), so all are variant. OpenAI family 015 was the closest call: it proves Haar limits of periodic torus packets using an unidentified measure-rigidity step, which is an equidistribution theorem about limits of periodic orbits, not a classification of A-invariant ergodic measures, so it is variant. Its AI role is coded generated from the lab's blanket statement that the vast majority of catalogue results came from the model; the credit is moot because the events are discarded.
judgement.doubts: EKL 2006 is coded unreviewed because the record does not open the journal version (search results say Annals) and checked_by is empty. It is pre-snapshot and a case, so it cannot make the status open_stale either way. The OpenAI AI attribution is a catalogue-wide sentence, not a statement about these particular manuscripts. Coverage of arXiv in the window relies on search results, not direct listings.
